changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retailers with stores, speaking to the COO and head of store operations: lead with 'One system for the tills and the website' and 'one customer, one basket', then walk through, step by step at the till, how an online order is returned in store. Show it live rather than describing it. Say 'the tills', not 'point of sale' or 'in-person payments'.
changes.why: M3 met silence and the head of store operations called it 'that's a diagram'. She then asked how a return works at the till, which we only described, and the customer's own phrases were sharper than ours.

changes.change: For store rollouts, add an accountability line built on the buyer's own worry, 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other'. State plainly who does installs and store rollout end to end. If a partner is involved, name it and position us as the single accountable party when something breaks.
changes.why: The deal turned when Tom said a partner would do the installs, which confirmed the COO's stated fear of two vendors pointing at each other.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For store-heavy buyers, replace 'see our customer stories' with an offer of a retail reference the buyer can call, ideally a store-rollout customer they recognise. Have the call ready to arrange before the buyer asks.
changes.why: Adyen named retailers the COO knew. When she asked 'can I talk to them?' we couldn't set up a call in time, so a story page is the wrong proof for this buyer.

changes.change: Add a proof point for store deals: a dated rollout plan that answers the buyer's checklist of 'Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills', presented by people who have done store rollouts.
changes.why: The customer asked for a dated rollout plan covering installs and old tills, and the competitor won credibility by bringing people who had done store rollouts.
